name: Efficiency-Ratio Forecast Gate (ML meta-filter)
description: Not a standalone strategy — a meta-filter. A logistic regression predicts whether TOMORROW will be a clean directional session (high efficiency ratio) or a chop session, using 15 measurements of how price has been moving. The forecast gates an existing strategy: skip the low-efficiency days entirely.
instrument: any — applied here to SPY daily

setup.description: Predict next-day efficiency ratio with logistic regression over 15 price-movement features. Rank days by predicted efficiency; trade only the days predicted to be clean/directional.

target.definition: Next session's directional efficiency = |Close - Open| / (High - Low).
target.label: 1 if next-day efficiency lands in the top tercile of the TRAINING distribution, else 0
target.note: A single-day Kaufman ER is degenerate (always 1.0), so the per-day efficiency must be the intraday |C-O|/(H-L) form. Multi-day features use the standard Kaufman ER = |net change over n| / sum(|daily changes| over n).

entry.long: base strategy signal AND predicted P(high efficiency) above the gate threshold

exit.rule: base strategy exit, OR the gate closing (predicted chop day)

claims_from_video.held_out: claimed to hold on 2 years the model never saw

falsifiable_claims: Predicted efficiency sorts next-day outcomes monotonically (low < medium < high) on expectancy and profit factor.
Gating out the low-predicted-efficiency tercile improves risk-adjusted return of the base strategy.
The improvement survives out-of-sample walk-forward, not just the fitted period.
honest_gaps: The reel never names the base strategy. 829 trades over the sample implies a far higher-frequency system than a daily SPY rule; we test the gate on the studio's reigning SPY champion (momentum), which trades far less often.
Reel weights are shown but we refit the model ourselves on training data only — using his published weights would be fitting to his sample, not ours.
Dollar expectancy is not comparable across strategies; we compare sharpe / return / drawdown instead.
notes: Model is refit on an expanding window with a strictly out-of-sample prediction block, so no future information enters the gate. Features are standardised on training-window statistics only.
